reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid OneCoin packages through a multi-level compensation structure in which earnings depend on personally recruiting participants, building left and right teams, and qualifying for deeper-generation commissions. It presents large income examples, including recovering half of a $5,000 package through two recruited $5,000 participants, describes payment to unlimited depth, and ends with a call to take action. The token discussion is secondary to the recruitment-driven solicitation.

take action now and welcome, to the world of cryptocurrency

opening.argument: The closing language qualifies the opportunity rather than promising effortless results: “It's not a miracle program” and it “will take work and persistence.” The speaker also describes bonuses as conditional on package level, personal referrals, and meeting qualifications, not as automatic payments to every viewer. The examples therefore do not establish a guaranteed return; they describe outcomes under stated conditions. A judge should distinguish an optimistic presentation from proof that the speaker promised certain earnings.

citations.quote: It's not a miracle program. Just like google and the others it will take work and persistence
as long as you qualify and you did 5 500
depending on the package that you have

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats conditional examples and an action-oriented ending as if they establish deception. But its cited $5,000 example is expressly framed as what could happen when the speaker refers two people at that package level, and its own “take action now” quote is followed by a suggestion to get questions answered. Those points show promotion, not that a return was guaranteed or that viewers were told results required no effort.

citations.quote: if you if you start at five grand right and you for two people for five grand
get back with the person that invited you to This video to get all of your questions the answered

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A work-and-persistence caveat does not undo the central pitch: viewers are shown compensation tied to packages and recruited teams, including a $2,500 total-bonus simulation after two $5,000 referrals. Calling that conditional still leaves the video presenting recruitment-linked earnings as an opportunity and urging viewers to act.

opening.argument: The video's dominant form is a training walkthrough: the speaker says it is training, shares a presentation, and explains how to read the compensation plan through worked examples. He walks through package levels, weekly caps, bonus calculations, and how left- and right-side volume is matched. The material is thus also an operational demonstration of a business compensation structure, not merely a bare promise of wealth. Its examples are introduced as explanations and simulations, which a careful judge should not mistake for documented payments or outcomes.

citations.quote: welcome to our training an understanding the details of our compensation plan
sometimes people need a visual to see how the structure of the team goes and how the points roll up
let's do a a simulation here of what happens when you start building a team

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's quotes establish that compensation is explained through referrals and team depth, but they do not establish that the video is only a recruitment pitch. It also spends substantial time teaching how the plan is calculated, including weaker-side matching, rollover points, package caps, and qualification rules. An instructional walkthrough can describe a compensation system without proving that its examples are actual results or that every claim is guaranteed.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The lesson is not neutral instruction detached from solicitation: it teaches viewers how to build the two teams and maximize earnings, then illustrates a $2,500 bonus based on two recruited package buyers. A slide format and explanatory calculations do not change what the training is teaching viewers to do.

citations.quote: how you can maximize the compensation plan
you were for two people at the five thousand dollar bonus

opening.argument: The supplied material describes paid packages, direct-sale commissions, and a compensation plan; it does not show a viewer being asked for passwords, payment credentials, or a particular transfer procedure. The speaker explains that the network bonus is calculated from weaker-side business volume and that matching bonuses depend on package and qualification. Those details support reading this as promotion of a package-based business opportunity. Even a persuasive, recruitment-oriented sales presentation does not by itself establish that the depicted transaction is fraudulent or that earnings are guaranteed.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to recruitment commissions and payment to unlimited depth, but those facts do not establish that a specific transaction is fraudulent. Its cited large-income example is hypothetical, and its call-to-action quote does not identify a payment destination or procedure. The distinction matters: the video explains package prices and how bonuses are calculated, while the supplied evidence does not show a credential request or a guaranteed payout to a buyer.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is not a password request or a guaranteed payout. The video makes earnings depend on recruiting package buyers, placing them on left and right teams, and qualifying for commissions across generations; it even says one can be paid when someone joins anywhere in the world. That is the recruitment-driven mechanism the prosecution identifies, regardless of whether credentials are requested.
